title: Take a hot jar of jam off the canner rack to cool: held by its glass, kept upright
instruction: Take the jar of jam off the canner rack to cool.
context: Home and small-batch commercial canning ends with hot, freshly sealed glass jars coming out of the canner. The guides all give the same rules for that step. University of Missouri Extension GH1452 ("Step by Step Successful Home Canning"): the jar lifter goes "below the neck of the jar (below the ring band of the lid)"; "Keep the jar upright at all times"; remove jars "being careful not to tilt the jars, and place them on a towel or cooling rack. Leave at least 1 inch of space between the jars during cooling. Avoid placing the jars on a cold surface." Michigan State University Extension: "Do not set hot jars on a cold surface ... either can cause the jars to break." Ball, the jar maker: "set upright on a towel. This will prevent jar breakage that can occur from temperature differences", and "do not place the hot jars down on cold, hard surfaces." UC Master Food Preservers describe the thermal-shock crack that runs round the lower part of a jar set on a cold surface.
setup: Positions in cm on the table from the midpoint between the two arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left; heights above the table top. The table stands for a stainless-steel prep bench. The canner's rack (perforated steel, 11 cm square, 2 cm tall, fixed) is centred at x 29, y 27; the hot jar stands on it, centred. The jar (and the one already cooling) is a 4 oz glass jelly jar of jam: a glass body 6.2 cm across and 5 cm tall, a 0.6 cm neck and a gold screw band 6.7 cm across and 1.2 cm tall over the lid, 6.8 cm tall in all, 0.21 kg. The folded tea towel (13 by 17 cm, 1 cm thick, fixed) is centred at x 32, y 9; the cooling jar stands on it at x 35, y 3.5. For real trials both jars are at room temperature, and the jar to move is filled with set jelly or sand to the same 0.21 kg, its band screwed on; the rack and towel are fixed to the table with double-sided tape. On camera each jar shows dark jam with clear glass headspace above it under the gold band.
scoring: The jar counts as on the towel while its base is on the towel (centre at least 1 cm inside its edges, at its top within 6 mm) and it is tilted under 15 degrees. Score 0 for the whole trial if the jar ever: comes to rest with its base on the bare steel bench (off the towel and the rack); is tilted more than 15 degrees; is lifted while a gripper's centre is at the screw band's height (held by the band); or falls off the bench; or if the cooling jar is moved more than 1 cm or tipped. At the end: 1.0 if the jar is on the towel with at least 2.5 cm of clear space between it and the cooling jar (success: that, at rest, for 1 s); 0 otherwise. Possible scores: 0, 1.0. On a real setup an overhead camera judges where the jar is set down and the gap to the cooling jar (marked on the towel); a side camera shows whether the jar was lifted by its band and whether it tipped past about 15 degrees.
reset_notes: Stand the jar back on the centre of the rack and the cooling jar on its mark on the towel. Run with -E object_jitter=0.
fidelity: The jars are rigid bodies (a glass body, neck and band as stacked cylinders, built with task-local hhcarry.py); the rack and the folded towel are fixed boxes, the towel rigid. Heat, glass stress and the lid's seal are not simulated: the guides' rules (where the jar is set down, how it is held, how far it tilts, the gap) are scored directly. The jars are small (4 oz) so the gripper can close round the glass; a canner is larger than its rack shown here.
scores: Dream-1: not run yet. Scripted demo (Isaac Sim, 17 Nov 2026): 1.0, step 241, held by its glass, upright, set on the towel. Naive (set on the cold steel bench): 0.0. Unsafe (lifted by its screw band): 0.0. Details in README.
